_comment: The commercial contract between the two Caster apps.
Caster is written twice - SwiftUI on iOS, Compose on Android - and the same
silent-drift problem that golden.json solves for game feel applies here for
money: a free limit loosened on one platform and not the other, or an ad cap
that is eight minutes on iPhone and three on Android, and nothing fails.
This file is the fixture both sides read. Change a value here and both go
red until they agree. Do not edit it to make a test pass - edit it when the
offer is meant to change, then change both apps.
Sibling of shared/parity/golden.json. Neither app owns it.

product._comment: One non-consumable. No tiers, no subscription.

_comment: What the free app allows. The games are never on this list: all six modes,
every sub-mode and every wheel entry stay free forever. Only the size of a
saved library is capped, and only when creating a new one - an existing
library over the cap is never hidden, trimmed or deleted.
One interstitial placement exists in the whole app: returning from a game
to the mode list. Never mid-round, never on a result reveal, never on a
Hot Potato pass, never on launch. Every clause below must pass.
Rewarded ads are opt-in and cosmetic only - they may grant a theme or a
sound pack for the session and nothing else. Gating functional capacity
behind watching an ad is an App Review 3.2.2(vi) rejection risk.
What the 3.99 buys. Kept here so the two paywalls cannot describe two
different products - and so neither of them can advertise something that
is not built yet. A false entry here becomes a false claim on a purchase
screen. Flip one to true on the day it works on both platforms, not on
the day it is planned.
